    One-sided cyclicity in the ray category of a distributive algebra #

    The ray-category axiom e) of Bongartz–Gabriel ("P(x, y) is cyclic over P(x, x) or over P(y, y)") for the BGRS ray category of a distributive algebra.

    • comm_of_chain: a local algebra with residue field k whose two-sided k-subspaces form a chain is k[γ], hence commutative.
    • hom_transit_or_cotransit: each Hom space between indecomposable projectives is uniformly transit or cotransit (Kupisch, GR 13.2).
    • ray_oneSided: axiom e) for the BGRS ray category; RaySmall.oneSidedCyclic transfers it to the small model.

      a * b = b * a

      A chain of two-sided ideals forces commutativity. A local k-algebra with residue field k and nilpotent radical whose two-sided k-subspaces form a chain is generated by one element, hence commutative.

        theorem LargeIndecomposable.ray_oneSided {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [Module.Finite k A] {ι : Type w} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k S.ProjectiveCategory] :
        OneSidedCyclic S.RayCategory

        Ray axiom e) (one-sided cyclicity). In the ray category of a distributive algebra, for each pair of objects either every two-sided multiple of a morphism is already a multiple on the target side, or every one is a multiple on the source side.
